head: Meta Muse Chrome extension puts the AI agent in your browser sidebar
dek: The Muse Chrome extension, Meta's AI agent in Chrome's side panel, is now official: Meta's chief AI officer Alexandr Wang announced it on X on 20 November. Muse chats with you next to any page and can shop, book travel and handle tasks in its own group of tabs.
details: The extension had appeared quietly in the Chrome Web Store, where TestingCatalog spotted it on 13 November; the listing shows about 200,000 users. It needs Chrome 137 or later and opens with Alt+Shift+C. Phone calls through Muse stay limited to paid subscribers in the US. Meta warns that Muse may take unexpected actions, so you should check in on it.
where: Chrome Web Store now, Chrome 137 or later; phone calls for paid US subscribers only
means: If you use Chrome, Muse can now work on websites for you while you watch, using the sites you're already logged into. Its activity may show up in your Google account and browsing history.
todo: Log out of any account you don't want Muse to use before connecting it. Turn on approvals so it asks before acting, and check its activity log. To stop it, click the page, press Esc or move the tab out of the Muse group.
